candidates.changed_node: B's raw CS_RANK($volume) penalty is multiplied by an informed-flow gate rebuilt around A's TS_DELTA($volume, 1)
candidates.rationale: BAD CROSS, mechanically unsatisfiable: parent B (CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK($volume)) has subtree sizes {1,2,5} and no 3-node subtree at all, so a child either takes B whole (shares 5 -> archive_subtree) or at most 2 (-> crossover_not_a_fusion). I took the 2-node option, which rejects earliest and at least leaves a non-restating expression on the log. Intended fusion, for the record: B docks every heavily traded name; A says the informative part of volume is whether volume shocks actually move the intraday range. So the turnover penalty is gated by informed-flow intensity - dock high-volume names only when their day-over-day volume shocks co-move with the open-to-high range, and leave uninformative churn alone. Donates TS_DELTA($volume, 1) (3 nodes) from A; the correlation is rebuilt on $high - $open at 63 days so the whole 8-node TS_CORR block of A is not restated.

candidates.changed_node: A's CS_RANK($volume) leg is re-scaled by B's TS_STD($return, 105) inside a single rank
candidates.rationale: BAD CROSS, same mechanical block: parent A here is the same CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK($volume) member with no 3-node subtree, so no child can share 3 nodes with it and stay under 4 shared with the archive. Intended fusion: A's turnover leg is really an attention/risk penalty, and B says the right scale for a name's price behaviour is 105-day realised vol. Multiplying volume by TS_STD($return, 105) before ranking makes it a risk-weighted turnover penalty, so quality is docked for names that trade heavily AND are volatile, not for large quiet names - a joint attention/risk control neither parent has. candidates.changed_node: B's vol-rank multiplier is replaced by a drawdown gate built on A's TS_MAX($high, 21)
candidates.rationale: Merton-style interaction: B penalises balance-sheet expansion scaled by short-horizon vol, A measures how stretched a name is inside its own 21-day high band. Neither links the two. The product says a 126-day leverage build-up is dangerous precisely when the equity has already fallen away from its recent high (asset value declining while liabilities grow) and is near-harmless for names printing new highs. Donates TS_MAX($high, 21) (3 nodes) from A and TS_DELTA($leverage, 126) (3 nodes) from B; the leverage leg is re-wrapped in CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK(...)) rather than B's CS_ZSCORE so the 4-node block is new, and the drawdown leg is rebuilt as TS_MAX/$high instead of A's TS_MAX-minus-TS_MEAN over vol*$close. candidates.changed_node: B's TS_CORR is re-aimed at the open-to-high range and multiplied by a 63-day rank of A's TS_STD($return, 5)
candidates.rationale: Regime conditioner on a participation kernel. B measures whether trading intensity co-moves with the daily range; A carries the short-horizon realised-vol state (TS_STD($return, 5)) that B has no access to. The product says the volume/range link is only tradeable when the name's own 5-day vol sits high within its 63-day history, and is noise on a quiet tape - a state variable B lacks and a participation measure A lacks. Donates TS_RANK($volume, 10) (3 nodes) from A(B-side kernel) and TS_STD($return, 5) (3 nodes) from A(4cf4ee72). The correlation is rebuilt on $high - $open at 21 days rather than $high - $low at 42, which also steps out of the very crowded TS_CORR(volume, $high - $low, w) family in the archive.

candidates.changed_node: B's CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)) penalty becomes a sign, gated by a 63-day rank of A's $high - $low
candidates.rationale: Conditioning, not a spread. B docks leverage growth uniformly across names; A says the tradeable state is how trading conditions rank within a name's own history. The product makes the leverage signal state-dependent: a build-up counts when the stock's intraday range is already elevated against its own 63-day distribution (risk being repriced) and flips/vanishes on a quiet tape. Donates $high - $low (3 nodes) from A and TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) (3 nodes) from B. SIGN is used because every bounded wrapper on that delta (CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE, ABS, MAX, unary minus) is already a live 4-node archive block, and it turns B's continuous penalty into a direction indicator whose ties are broken by the continuous range rank.

candidates.changed_node: A's leverage delta is crossed with a 42-day downside-return share rebuilt from B's MIN($return, 0)
candidates.rationale: Downside-tail interaction. A carries balance-sheet risk with no return-distribution term; B carries a downside-vol share but ties it to 68-day momentum. The cross puts leverage growth against the share of a name's total absolute return that came from down days - a semivariance/skew proxy - so a lever-up is punished hardest in firms already exposed to left-tail moves, and discounted in firms whose moves are one-sided up. Donates TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) (3 nodes) from A and MIN($return, 0) (3 nodes) from B, rebuilt as a 42-day downside share (TS_SUM instead of B's TS_STD, and normalised by TS_SUM(ABS($return), 42), a window not used anywhere in the archive) so B's 5-node TS_STD(MIN(...), 68) block is not restated.

candidates.changed_node: B's roa delta is reduced to a direction and signs A's 68-day cumulative return z-score
candidates.rationale: Fundamental-momentum confirmation. B pairs a roa change with an accrual leg and a long price rank; A pairs 68-day momentum with a downside-vol share. The product is a confirmation/divergence indicator: large and positive when a roa improvement is being priced (or a deterioration is being sold), and negative where price and fundamentals disagree - which is the mispricing case. candidates.rationale: Pricing-in interaction between the two parents' distinctive legs. B's efficiency term (TS_DELTA($asset_turnover, 63)) never meets a price variable - it only meets roa inside a MIN and an accrual spread; A's long price-position term only ever multiplies the accrual leg. prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.
